_comment: Ground truth for calibration run 2026-07-26-r2. Blinded: this file never enters the dispatch directory (/tmp/ledger-dispatch, single commit 26231da348a3). Match rule per docs/benchmark-protocol.md: file basename + exact category + line within tolerance. Corpus deliberately harder than 2026-07-13-r1 per that run's ceiling-effect note: it plants concurrency (D1), cross-file symptom-far-from-cause (D2, D4), and a no-op-implementation leak (D7).

defects.description: append() reads next_offset() under a read lock, releases it, then inserts under a write lock; two concurrent appends observe the same offset and B1's uniqueness/density guarantee breaks. Symptom surfaces later as a duplicate/skipped offset in replay.

capture() discards retention_watermark and records the index max as last_applied; B5 requires the checkpoint to sit at or above the watermark, so retention can reclaim the segment the checkpoint names and replay then cannot find it.
push() seals on `len() > max_records` after the push, so a segment holds max_records+1 records, violating B3.
relative_position() computes `absolute - seg.base_offset` with no check that the offset belongs to that segment; a mismatched segment underflows u64 and yields a huge position, violating B8.
replay_from() uses `if let Ok(..)` and silently skips undecodable records, returning Ok; B4 requires aborting with ReplayError::Corrupt.

open() guards checkpoint_threshold instead of the segment capacity and then coerces max_records_per_segment with .max(1), so a zero capacity is silently accepted rather than rejected with ZeroSegmentCapacity per B2.
prune_before() ignores its watermark and drops nothing, so index entries for reclaimed records accumulate without bound, violating B7.
should_checkpoint() returns `pending < threshold`, the inverse of B6; checkpoints fire only while under the threshold and stop once one is due.
